title: Louis and Duke were unteachable originals
summary: Nobody taught Louis or Duke their ways; Billie Holiday, Sinatra and Crosby all listened to Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And these are things that he naturally had. Nobody taught him that. He didn't learn that from anybody. Those were -- it was just Louis. He was just Louis. It's just like Duke, you know, and the smile that he would have out there and his talk. Nobody could teach Duke anything about speaking. It was him, because it wouldn't sound right, that same thing

he said coming from somebody else. If he wrote it and gave it to the average guy to say, it just wouldn't sound right. That was Duke. That was him. That's how he felt inside. Well, this is the way Louis was, how he expressed himself, and these are many of the things that I learned from Louis and a lot of other guys there in front of -- because, let's face it, all the greatest singers, jazz singers all learned from him.

Billie Holiday said all she listened to was Louis and Bessie Smith and people like that. Sinatra said he listened to him and Billie Holiday. And Bing said he listened to Louis and he -- who else, man, is there, you know?
